statement: Four books stand on a shelf. Green is left of red. Blue is right of red. Yellow is between green and red. Which book is third from the left?

choices.misconception: I read the shelf from the right end and also forgot the yellow book, so from the right I had blue, red, green.
I counted from the right end of the shelf instead of from the left.
I forgot the yellow book, so I lined up green, red, blue and took blue as the third book.
I thought 'between' did not say exactly where the yellow book goes, so I decided the order was not fixed.

hints: Draw four spaces and place the books one clue at a time.
Draw the shelf as a row of four spaces. Put green before red, blue after red, then fit yellow into the gap between green and red. Only one order uses all four spaces.
Green must come before yellow, which comes before red, and blue comes after red. So from the left the order is green, yellow, red, blue.

solutions.reliable: Green is somewhere left of red, and yellow is between them, so we have green, yellow, red in that order. Blue is to the right of red, so it goes last. The shelf from the left reads green, yellow, red, blue, and the third book is red. The transferable idea: draw the line and place the items, rather than holding them in your head.

whyOnTest: Ordering clues test turning words like left of and between into a drawn line, and counting from the correct end.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
